regime_context: The detector shows a broad leadership rotation concentrated at the top of Semiconductors/Memory: 'Memory, HBM & Storage' is the clear leader (score 2.34, margin ~0.60 over AI Infrastructure), with a non-dominant, distributed structure (one_narrative=false, absorption 0.32). The validated edge here is drawdown/shake-out control via the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps=true), not return forecasting; rank-IC is ~0 and rotation-timing is display-only. Track record shows decent hit rate (0.711) but near-coinflip directional accuracy (0.526), so conviction should stay low-to-medium.
emerging_watch: Watching whether 'AI Infrastructure' (challenger, score 1.745) closes the 0.60 margin against the Memory/HBM leader — I am watching for a CONFIRMED handoff (AI Infrastructure overtaking Memory, HBM & Storage in score for 3+ consecutive days) rather than predicting it; the watch retires if the margin widens back above 0.75 in the leader's favor.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The leader is eligible and trend-gate-passing, with solid but not extreme breadth (0.75) and a non-crowded texture (crowding_z 0.53). It is the prevailing narrative (headline weight 0.25) and the rotation leader, with a healthy 0.60 margin over the challenger. The absolute-trend gate supports holding it on the stay-power/vol-control leg. This is a trend-continuation lean, not a momentum-buy: I am expressing the view that the theme remains the place leadership is concentrating, and that the gate's drawdown-avoidance leg is the reason to stay with it rather than rotate away.
evidence: rank 1, score 2.34, eligible=true (trend-gate leg supports exposure)
headline weight 0.25, rotation leader with margin 0.595
crowding_z 0.53 — not crowded, no size-down flag
durability_bar 0.68, hurst_tag mixed (trend-health middling, so modest conviction)
theses.dissent: The hurst_tag is mixed and durability_bar is only 0.68, so the trend is not cleanly persistent; memory is a highly cyclical sub-industry where leadership can roll over fast on capacity/price headlines, and cross-sectional momentum has no forward edge.

falsifier.text: SMH (proxy) lags the S&P 500 by 5% or falls out of the top-3 rank by score before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: AI Semiconductors
theses.thesis: AI Semiconductors shows the strongest trend-health texture in the list (hurst_tag=trend, durability_bar 0.85, breadth 0.917) and is eligible and non-crowded (crowding_z 0.69). This is the trend-gate leg at its cleanest — high persistence plus broad participation. It supports a continuation lean even though its rank (5) trails the memory leader.
evidence: hurst_tag=trend, durability_bar 0.85 — cleanest persistence in the list
theses.dissent: It shares the SMH proxy with the leader and other semis, so it is not genuinely independent; the high durability read could simply be a late-cycle extension of the same AI capex trade that is already crowded at the aggregate level, and momentum rank itself has no predictive edge.

falsifier.text: SMH lags the S&P 500 by 5% or the AI Semiconductors score drops below eligible mid-pack before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity has the strongest combination of trend-health (hurst_tag=trend, durability_bar 0.76) and breadth (0.90) among the top ranks, and it is eligible. It is flagged crowded (crowding_z 1.82), which is a SIZE-DOWN caution only — per guardrails I do not fade or short it, and I cap conviction rather than lean against it.
evidence: crowding_z 1.82, crowded=true — size-down caution, not a fade
theses.dissent: The crowding flag (z 1.82) is the highest in the top ranks and attention/flow spikes in thematic ETFs often mark local tops; the only validated edge for this theme is the drawdown gate, and a crowded trend name can shake out hardest.
